title: Opportunistic kernel shim concurrency leads to KV-slot striping and softmax jitter
creator: Asha Patel
description: Summary: After merging the opportunistic kernel shim that enables on-the-fly kernel swaps for latency-sensitive requests, we've observed non-deterministic output (token-level differences), occasional high-softmax variance, and KV cache slot fragmentation under steady-state concurrent traffic. The issue manifests during mixed prefill+decode workloads when kernel selection changes mid-request and concurrent requests race to update shared KV metadata structures. This ticket tracks root-cause analysis, a safe short-term mitigation, and a robust fix plus tests and rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Reproducer that triggers KV-slot misalignment and numeric drift reliably in CI-scale environment
Root cause documented and agreed by runtime and infra leads
Fix merged that prevents concurrent kernel-switch races without regressing throughput by >10% on typical workloads
End-to-end regression test added to nightly that asserts deterministic logits for seeded workloads and KV integrity checks
Canary deployed to hosted with fallback policy and monitoring alerts for 72h without incidents
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Deploy runtime-1.24 with opportunistic kernel-shim feature flag enabled
2) Use a mixed workload generator: 40% long-prefill requests (seq_len 1024) and 60% streaming decode requests (avg 64 tokens), concurrency=120; target a single GPU pool
3) Enable dynamic kernel selection on attention layers (fused <-> fallback) and low-latency scheduling so kernel swap may occur during decode
4) Run for 30 minutes and capture token-by-token logits for seeded prompts from multiple concurrent clients
5) Observe token-level divergence across runs and jumpy softmax magnitudes in traces; confirm KV slot offset annotations mismatch between prefill and decode phases in logs
investigation_log: 2026-03-10: Initial report from SRE on hosted cluster showing increased token-delta alerts for customer test harness (repro rate ~1/2000 requests). Assigned to Miguel.
2026-03-11: Local repro created using synthetic harness; divergence rate increased when kernel migration window overlaps KV write of concurrent streams.
2026-03-11: Heap snapshot reveals KV metadata header contains stale 'slot_base' values for ~3% of inflight requests after kernel swap sequence.

2026-03-12: Added additional tracing in kernel selection path; found race between KernelSelector::prepare_swap() and PrefillKVWriter::commit_metadata() where commit order is not serialized leading to interleaved slot indices.

2026-03-12: Numeric analysis shows low-confidence tokens have higher softmax variance (0.6x-1.8x) post-migration and that loss of positional KV continuity amplifies rounding differences across kernels resulting in different top-token choices.

2026-03-12: Confirmed issue reproduces only when (a) opportunistic kernel swapping is enabled, (b) KV cache is shared across requests (shared pool mode), and (c) multi-threaded prefill+decode scheduling allows overlap. Standalone single-request runs are unaffected.
root_cause_hypothesis: Concurrent kernel swap is racing with KV metadata writes: the opportunistic shim triggers a kernel binary switch which updates per-request KV layout assumptions. If a prefill thread commits its KV metadata slightly before the kernel swap completes, another decode thread may compute offsets based on the old layout and write into incorrectly striped slots. This causes KV fragmentation and compounding rounding differences when kernels use different accumulation/quantization paths.
proposed_fix: 1) Make kernel migration an atomic handoff w.r.t. KV metadata by introducing a versioned KV header and a small lockless epoch counter that prefill/commit paths check before/after writes. 2) On mismatch, the writer will retry with the current epoch and, if necessary, perform a lightweight reconciliation pass that consolidates fragmented slots. 3) Conservative short-term mitigation: disable opportunistic kernel swaps for shared KV pools (feature-flag off) until fix is validated.
rollback_plan: If canary shows increased latency or new errors: revert opportunistic kernel-shim flag in hosted clusters and re-enable previous selection behavior; immediate hotfix to restore serialized kernel migration path.
regression_tests: Deterministic seeded-run test asserting identical logits across 50 sequential runs under concurrency=100
KV-integrity checker asserting no overlapping slot ranges and contiguous slot allocation after a mix of prefill/decode cycles
Fuzz harness that toggles kernel selection mid-request and asserts state invariants
Throughput microbench comparing throughput with opportunistic-on vs opportunistic-off to ensure < 10% perf regression
rollout_plan: 1) Land fix behind feature flag in runtime branch. 2) Run extended CI with fuzz harness and nightly KV-integrity suite. 3) Canary deploy to hosted-us-west with 5% traffic for 48h, auto-fallback to prior runtime on error thresholds (token-delta alerts > 0.1% or latency P99 regress > 20%). 4) Expand to Dedicated pools with isolated KV allocations then full rollout.
monitoring_and_alerting: New metric: kv.slot_retries.count (should be near 0 in steady state)
Token-delta alert threshold tuned for seeded regressions; alert if divergence > 0.05% per hour
Softmax-variance histogram per model-version; anomaly detection to catch drift spikes
Canary dashboard card showing kernel-swap-rate, kv_reconcile_count, and request-error-rate
